name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: A large-scale multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consisting of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. December 22, 2020.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created from LibriVox audiobook data, most of which is based on Project Gutenberg text data. The authors selected English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, and Polish based on audiobook hours and availability of corresponding text sources. Audiobooks were downloaded using LibriLight tools, downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz, segmented into 10-20 second clips using acoustic models and silence intervals, pseudo labels were generated, original text sources were downloaded or manually retrieved, and transcripts were recovered by matching pseudo labels to source texts.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The training data is lower than the data presented from LibriVox because the text source for some audiobooks may not have been downloaded, candidate labels were filtered during transcript retrieval, or data was filtered while creating validation/test splits.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read-speech audiobook audio from LibriVox and corresponding book text sources from gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, and other online sources; for language models, source text was taken from Project Gutenberg books.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio was segmented into 10-20 second segments by running inference to obtain token timestamps and splitting at the longest silence between 10 and 20 seconds, or at 20 seconds if no silence was found. Source text was split into overlapping 1250-word documents with stride 1000. Candidate transcripts were retrieved using TF-IDF similarity on bigrams and Smith-Waterman alignment, then filtered if WER with pseudo labels was greater than 40%. Numbers in matched text were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels, and heuristics were used to handle hyphens and apostrophes.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters such as punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, and escape symbols, removal of end-of-line hyphenation and joining split words, and filtering characters outside a valid unicode range based on each language's orthography. Books with corrupted metadata, missing title or speaker/author information, multiple speakers, or duplicate versions were removed for split creation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo labels for segmented audio were generated by beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model on acoustic models. Final transcripts were obtained by matching pseudo labels to source book text using TF-IDF retrieval and Smith-Waterman alignment. For high quality development and test sets, human transcribers listened to the audio while viewing the transcript and corrected only clear and obvious errors.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Candidate transcripts were filtered out if the WER between the candidate transcript and pseudo label was greater than 40%. For development and test sets, transcript quality was assessed by comparing generated transcripts with human rated transcripts, and WER between generated transcript and human rated transcript was reported for each language.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere, acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable Convolutions with ASG loss, 4-gram language models, TF-IDF similarity on bigrams, Smith-Waterman alignment, pdftotext, gender classifier based on SVM with RBF kernel
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be made freely available for anyone at http://www.openslr.org. The paper also states that language model training data, pre-built language models, pretrained models, and training recipes will be made available. No updating timeframe or deprecation policy is specified.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors believe the dataset will promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and in multilingual ASR, and open new avenues in ASR and Text-To-Speech research.
rai:dataBiases: To avoid potential bias from human transcribing, transcribers were asked to correct only clear and obvious errors. Development and test speakers were balanced in gender and duration. The paper notes English is the dominant language in LibriVox source data.
rai:dataLimitations: For non-English languages, automatically extracting text sources was challenging because of diverse domains and invalid or redirected links, requiring manual approaches. The number replacement solution using pseudo labels is not perfect because pseudo labels may not always have the correct transcription. Training data is reduced because some text sources were unavailable, some candidate labels were filtered, and some data was filtered during split creation. Polish language model decoding was negatively impacted by a 13% OOV rate.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for speech research, especially Automatic Speech Recognition and Text-To-Speech research. It provides train, development, and test splits, as well as limited supervision training subsets of 10 hours, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets for low-resource training benchmarks. Development and test sets are intended for evaluation, and language model training data and pre-built language models are also released.
